title: 1970 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) the median from vertex \(A\) is perpendicular to the median from vertex \(B.\) If the lengths of sides \(AC\) and \(BC\) are \(6\) and \(7,\) respectively, then the length of side \(AB\) is:

solutions.text:
Place the centroid at the origin. Let the position vectors of \(A\) and \(B\) be \(u\) and \(v.\) The two medians lie along \(u\) and \(v,\) so \(u\cdot v=0.\) Also the centroid condition gives \(C=-u-v.\)

Let \(U=|u|^2\) and \(V=|v|^2.\) Then \[ AC^2=|2u+v|^2=4U+V=36 \] and \[ \begin{aligned} BC^2&=|u+2v|^2\\ &=U+4V=49. \end{aligned} \] Adding appropriate multiples gives \(U+V=17.\) Finally, \[ AB^2=|u-v|^2=U+V=17, \] so \(AB=\sqrt{17}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Place the centroid at the origin and let the position vectors of \(A,B\) be perpendicular vectors \(u,v\)
